details.eduWhat: What is Forward P/E and How is it Calculated?
details.eduWhatDesc: Forward Price-to-Earnings measures the current stock price relative to expected future earnings per share (EPS) over the next fiscal year or next 12 rolling months (NTM):
details.eduFormula: Forward P/E = Current Stock Price / Forecasted Next FY EPS
details.eduHow: How is it calculated and by whom?
details.eduHowDesc: It is based on consensus estimates compiled from dozens of professional equity research analysts (Wall Street & European financial institutions) covering the company. As analysts revise their profit projections following quarterly earnings and company guidance, the forward EPS and resulting Forward P/E update dynamically.
details.eduComparisonDesc: Trailing P/E reflects audited historical performance over the last 12 months (TTM). Forward P/E looks into the future. A Forward P/E significantly lower than Trailing P/E indicates analysts anticipate strong earnings growth. If higher, earnings contraction is expected.
details.eduCaveatDesc: Forward P/E is only as reliable as analyst projections. If economic slowdowns, unexpected tariff shifts, or margin compressions occur, consensus earnings may be downgraded, making an apparently 'cheap' forward valuation illusory.
details.consensusTableSubtitle: Detailed multi-horizon EPS forecasts and research coverage
details.whoAreAnalysts: Where do these projections come from and who builds the consensus?
details.whoAreAnalystsDesc: Estimations are authored by professional sell-side financial analysts at major investment banks and brokerage firms (e.g. Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, BNP Paribas Exane, Kepler Cheuvreux, Société Générale). Their proprietary DCF and operational models forecast future sales, margins, and net earnings per share. Global financial data aggregators (LSEG / Refinitiv, FactSet, S&P Global) collect, normalize, and average these research models into the consensus mean displayed on Yahoo Finance.
details.multipleHorizons: Why are there multiple forward earnings horizons?
details.multipleHorizonsDesc: Analysts project across several horizons: Current Year (FY0), Next Fiscal Year (FY1, the canonical Forward P/E benchmark), and Year N+2 (FY2). The standard Forward P/E multiple uses FY1 (or the next 12 rolling months, NTM). As time progresses, earlier quarters are actualized and the consensus rolls forward.
details.dispersionDesc: The spread between the lowest and highest analyst estimates reflects market certainty or cyclicality. A tight spread means high predictability; a wide spread indicates volatile earnings. In addition, the 30-day revision balance shows whether Wall Street has been recently upgrading or slashing profit targets.
details.etfConsensusNote: For ETFs and index funds, Forward P/E represents the market-cap weighted average of the hundreds of underlying constituent stocks in the index basket.
